title: Peace Symbol Emoji ☮️ Meaning, Origin, and Hippie Vibes
description: The ☮️ peace symbol emoji stands for peace, anti-war protest, and 1960s counterculture. Learn where the sign came from and how it differs from ✌️ and 🕊️.
summary: The ☮️ peace symbol emoji shows the circle-and-lines peace sign. It stands for peace, nonviolence, and opposition to war, and it evokes 1960s hippie culture. People use it in calls for peace, in retro and festival aesthetics, and to wish calm on a tense conversation.
meaning: ☮️ reproduces one of the most recognized symbols of the twentieth century. It was designed in 1958 by the British artist Gerald Holtom for a march against nuclear weapons, and was adopted by the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament. Holtom based it on the flag semaphore signals for the letters N and D, for nuclear disarmament, set inside a circle.

The sign crossed the Atlantic and became the emblem of the 1960s anti-war movement and of hippie counterculture generally. That history gives the emoji two tones. One is sincere: people post ☮️ during wars, after violence, and on occasions such as the International Day of Peace to express a wish for conflict to end. The other is nostalgic, calling up tie-dye, VW vans, and music festivals.

In everyday messages the emoji mostly signals a mellow attitude. "Peace and love ☮️" closes a note warmly; "keeping the ☮️" means staying out of drama. It can be a way to step back from an argument without conceding. Wellness and yoga accounts use it with other spiritual symbols for inner peace, though the sign itself is political in origin, not religious.

It is used far less than the ✌️ hand, which covers "peace" as a casual greeting or goodbye. ☮️ is the choice when someone means the concept or wants the vintage look. Its long association with protest also means some audiences read it as a political statement, even when it is posted as decoration.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Retro outfits, festival photos, and 60s or 70s themed parties are common settings, often with ✌️, 🌼, and 🌈. Travel and nature posts use it for a sense of calm. Shops selling vintage clothing and vinyl records include it in bios to signal their style.

contexts.label: In activism and news
contexts.body: During armed conflicts, vigils, and anti-war demonstrations, ☮️ appears in posts calling for ceasefires and diplomacy, frequently beside 🕊️. Schools and community groups use it around peace-themed observances. In these settings it is earnest, and joking replies can come across as disrespectful.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends send it to defuse tension ("not fighting about this ☮️"), to sign off, or to describe a blissful day. It can also be gently ironic, used by someone pretending to be serene while clearly annoyed. The surrounding words tell you which.

combos.meaning: Peace and love, the familiar hippie-era pairing.
A hope for peace, especially in the context of war.
Peace doubled, in a relaxed or retro mood.

confusedWith.difference: ✌️ is the two-finger gesture people use for "peace out," selfies, or the number two. It is casual and personal. ☮️ is the printed symbol and suits statements about peace as an idea or a retro aesthetic.
🕊️ is a white dove, often with an olive branch, an older emblem of peace with religious roots that is also used for mourning. ☮️ comes from a modern protest movement and carries no religious meaning.

☯️ represents balance between complementary forces in Chinese philosophy. Both are circular and appear together in spiritual-themed posts, yet ☮️ is about ending conflict and ☯️ about harmony of opposites.

avoid: Do not reply with a breezy ☮️ to someone describing real harm from violence or war; add words that show you understand.
Avoid treating it as apolitical in every setting, since many people read it as an anti-war statement.
Do not use it to shut down a legitimate complaint by implying the other person is disturbing the peace.
design: A circle containing a vertical line with two shorter lines branching downward from its center. Most platforms show the symbol in white on a purple square, the same tile used for religious and astrological symbols; some render it in other colors. Without emoji styling the base character appears as a plain black outline.

faqs.q: What does the peace symbol actually stand for?
faqs.a: It combines the semaphore positions for N and D, meaning nuclear disarmament, inside a circle. Gerald Holtom created it in 1958 for British anti-nuclear protesters. It later became a general sign for peace.

faqs.q: What does ☮️ mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually a laid-back attitude: no drama, good vibes, or a friendly goodbye. It can also be a way of ending a disagreement. It has no romantic meaning.

faqs.q: Is the peace symbol religious or anti-religious?
faqs.a: Neither. It was made for a political campaign. Claims that it has occult or anti-Christian origins have circulated for decades but do not match the documented history of its design.
✌️ is a hand gesture used casually in greetings and photos. ☮️ is the graphic emblem associated with protest and the 1960s. Use the hand to say bye and the symbol to talk about peace.
The character had long existed in Unicode as a text symbol and gained emoji status in 2015 as part of Emoji 1.0, the first formal list of emoji.
